Becomes 03L/21R when the new runway opens.
OSM way 718668626 within 10 m; OurAirports 16/17 m. ends[0]=06, correct.

No source publishes threshold coordinates (not in OSM, OurAirports or any page I could read; the Perth Airport PDFs return 403 to this tool, text seen only via search snippets). Rebuilt the geometry from the MDP Vol A s6 wording as quoted in search results: parallel to 03L/21R, 2,000 m separation, 3,000 m long, 'moved further south by 1,030 metres compared to the existing main runway (03L/21R) northern threshold' (2018 redesign that shortened it 3,800 to 3,000 m to stay clear of Munday Swamp). Construction on the stated reading (northern end 1,030 m south of the 21 threshold, runway running south) gives N end [115.98643,-31.94193], S end [115.97878,-31.96811]: ours differ by about 10 m. Our placement is therefore the exact application of the published numbers, and its real accuracy is that of the published figures (approximate 'about 1,030 m' stagger and nominal 2 km spacing, probably +/-100-200 m, not the 500 m feared). One snippet mentions 2,700 m length; most sources (Wikipedia, MDP) say 3,000 m. The only other reading (southern end 1,030 m south of the northern threshold, runway running north) would put the north end ~3 km further north at [115.99407,-31.91574] and conflicts with the 'as far south as practicable' intent and the 'between Terminal 1 and Abernethy Road' description. Status Oct 2026: under construction, completion 2028 (Perth Airport 4 Dec 2025 article 'New runway project takes off'); Wikipedia says 2029.

flightPaths.departs: Preferred departure runway (about 57-60% of all departures; 61% daytime, 64% night in 2012). DAP initial track 196 magnetic (about 194 true), then at 1,000 ft but not before the runway end ATC turns aircraft: about two thirds (eastern states, NZ) turn LEFT to the east (SID legs track 107 magnetic, roughly 90 degrees of left turn), about 40% (west/north/north-west: Africa, Middle East, Asia, Pilbara) turn RIGHT to the west (SID leg track 280 magnetic, roughly 85 degrees right); some SIDs fly straight on 196 to AVBAD/JANDO (south) before turning. So turns are large (about 85-90 degrees), not 40, and start within a few km, not after 6 km. Exact turn distance is not published (waypoint coordinates not in the text I could read).
flightPaths.arrives: Jet arrivals are aligned with the runway at least 10 km out and fly a straight 3-degree final (Airservices). Our 26 km straight-in is longer than the published ~10 km alignment; before that, arrivals join from RNAV arrival waypoints (KABLI/JULIM/SAPKO/LAVEX arrival charts), so the far end of our 26 km line is not where aircraft actually fly. Runway 21 arrivals from the south may be flown as a visual left turn to final for aircraft at or below 45,000 kg; from the west via WOOFY to 6 NM final.
sources: https://www.crc.id.au/xplane/charts/DAPS-2026-JUL-09/Perth%20(YPPH).pdf (mirror of Airservices DAP, SID pages PPHDP01/03/08, magnetic tracks, variation 2 W)

flightPaths.departs: Used in northerly flow (about 32% of departures in 2012). DAP initial track 016 magnetic (about 014 true) straight to MIDLA (far north, near RAAF Pearce airspace), then SIDs turn LEFT to track 280 (west) or RIGHT to track 087 (east). Airservices: 'Aircraft with westerly and northerly destinations will turn left'; right turns only when they do not conflict with Runway 06 traffic. Overnight, when Pearce airspace is inactive, aircraft take shorter tracks over military airspace to the north. Turn point distance is not published here (SIDs go straight to MIDLA, probably well beyond 6 km); radar vectors from 1,000 ft are common.

flightPaths.departs: Less-used departure end, used for crosswinds in northerly flow (Priority 1 departure in northerly flow when it does not conflict with 03). DAP initial track 061 magnetic; at 1,000 ft turn LEFT direct MIDLA (about 45 degrees left, then west) or RIGHT toward ALWYN/HOVEA (track 079-094, a gentle right).
flightPaths.arrives: Priority 2 (less preferred) arrival runway: straight in from the west, aircraft 'track west of the coast to conduct a straight in approach'; the south-west end is close to housing.
sources: https://www.crc.id.au/xplane/charts/DAPS-2026-JUL-09/Perth%20(YPPH).pdf (mirror of Airservices DAP, SID pages PPHDP01/03/08, magnetic tracks, variation 2 W)

flightPaths.departs: Least preferred departure runway (Priority 2; about 7% of 2012 departures). DAP initial track 241 magnetic, at 1,500 ft turn LEFT direct AVBAD (south, roughly 45 degrees left) or continue on 241 to TUVBA before turning, so mostly straight or left; the housing at the south-western end is the reason it is avoided.
flightPaths.arrives: Priority 1 arrival runway in southerly flow (21/24); from the south via waypoint SPUDO. Straight final.
sources: https://www.crc.id.au/xplane/charts/DAPS-2026-JUL-09/Perth%20(YPPH).pdf (mirror of Airservices DAP, SID pages PPHDP01/03/08, magnetic tracks, variation 2 W)

flightPaths.departs: FUTURE runway: no flight paths published. Airservices says new flight paths are being designed; preliminary design engagement in early 2027, further engagement late 2027, final flight paths in 2028 (https://engage.airservicesaustralia.com/perth). Nothing to recommend yet; the map's fans are placeholders.

No curfew; 24-hour operation, voluntary Noise Abatement Procedures only (NAP 1 preferred runways, NAP 2 preferred flight paths, NAPs are not mandatory). Priority 1: arrive 21/03/24, depart 21/03/06. Priority 2: arrive 06, depart 24. Jets must stay at or above 5,000 ft AGL over residential areas where possible; turboprops 3,000 ft. Perth is NOT an over-water airport; military airspace north/north-west (RAAF Pearce) is used by civil aircraft when inactive, mostly nights and weekends. Morning departure burst from about 5 am prefers Runway 21. The 2014 review floated reciprocal ops (21 arrivals + 03 departures at night) but no source shows it adopted.
Not jet airports; map outlines only (noModel). No check needed.
